standard.title: Respond to stories and characters
standard.description: respond to stories and share feelings and thoughts about their events and characters
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have listened to and engaged with stories. They have not yet been explicitly asked to formulate and share a personal response — to reflect on their feelings about events and characters and communicate this response in a deliberate way.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can share personal feelings and thoughts about story events and characters through multiple modes — oral, drawing or beginning writing — connecting events and characters to their own experiences.

nodes.label: Stories prompt feelings
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify a feeling evoked by a story or character and name it.
nodes.minimum_width: Name one feeling a story evoked (e.g. 'I felt happy/sad/scared') when discussing a text.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and name feelings evoked by story events and characters; discuss what caused the feeling — connecting events to emotional responses.
wider: Compare feelings evoked by different types of stories — funny stories, sad stories, scary stories — and discuss what makes each evoke different responses
Explore how characters' feelings in a story differ from student responses to those same events
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot identify and name a feeling evoked by a story, they have no content for the sharing and mode-selection task in Node 2 — the deliberate response that Node 2 requires is built on the raw material of named feelings from this node.

response_modes.reason: Students need to encounter multiple stories and name feelings across them — a single story is insufficient to build the habit of noticing and naming emotional responses. Accumulating examples is what makes the naming automatic.

success_criteria: Student can name at least one feeling evoked by a story event or character.
Student can connect the feeling to a specific event or character in the text.

nodes.label: Responses can be shared in multiple ways
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share a personal response to a story through drawing, beginning writing or oral sharing — choosing a mode appropriate to the response.
nodes.minimum_width: Share a response to one story through drawing or oral expression.
nodes.typical_width: Respond to stories using drawing and beginning forms of writing to express personal responses; discuss events and characters, connecting them to personal experiences; share responses orally with peers.
wider: Respond to the same story through multiple modes — oral, drawing, movement or drama — and compare what each allows
Create a shared class response text (collaborative drawing or dictated writing) about a favourite story
Respond to First Nations Australian stories and discuss responses with attention to cultural context

response_modes.reason: Students bring together: having a personal response, reflecting on it, and translating it into a shareable form (drawing, writing, speech). The coordination of these acts is the learning.

success_criteria: Student can share a feeling or thought about a story event or character through drawing, speech or beginning writing.
Student can connect their response to a specific event or character.
Student can explain their response when asked — articulating why they felt or thought that.
